subject: Proposal: 2-year step-up commitment with safety valve & auto-align option
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Zhou <alex@spectrahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: 2-year step-up commitment with safety valve & auto-align option

Alex — following our call this morning, attached is a compact proposal that aligns to what we discussed: a 24-month step-up commitment with an embedded safety valve (true-up window) and an optional auto-align to your fiscal year at renewal. High-level summary below, details in the attached PDF and MAP (mutual_action_plan_spectra.xlsx).

Highlights:
- Structure: 2-year step-up (Year 1: 60% of peak forecast; Year 2: 100% of projected peak).
- Ramp cadence: quarterly step increases tied to usage milestones (see pricing_breakdown_v2.xlsx).
- Safety valve (triggers): if actual avg+95th usage > committed buckets for two consecutive months, a one-time true-up applies (limited to 20% of committed increase) to avoid throttling during growth spikes.
- Auto-align option: on renewal Redwood can pro-rate and rebase the commitment to align with Spectra fiscal year (if elected, applies only at renewal).
- Canary / capacity reservation: we recommend a Q4 canary slot (reserved burst capacity) for the first production rollout.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Review the attached proposal + MAP internally.
2) Tell us whether you want the auto-align option enabled at renewal (we can model proration).
3) If procurement is ready, Marissa can draft a DocuSign-ready amendment and PO language.

Attachments: Redwood_StepUp_Proposal_v1.pdf, mutual_action_plan_spectra.xlsx

Thanks — happy to sync on a quick 20-min follow-up.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0162

Alex — wanted to add the concrete accounting and operational details Grace flagged so you have them for finance/procurement. Quick answers below and a short pricing snapshot (see attached pricing_breakdown_v2.xlsx for cell-level math).

Safety valve / billing treatment:
- Trigger detection: platform monitors monthly token usage vs committed buckets. If threshold breached for two consecutive months, Redwood issues a true-up invoice for the incremental committed capacity.
- Invoicing: true-up is invoiced in the next billing cycle after the second breach month (no retroactive credit). We can optionally convert the invoice to a quarterly amortized charge if you prefer smoother GAAP treatment (we'll need a signed amendment).

Auto-align option:
- If elected at renewal, Redwood will rebase the committed buckets to match your fiscal-year profile and apply a pro-rated credit/charge for the remainder of the term. This is a one-time rebase at renewal unless otherwise agreed in writing.

Canary capacity:
- Lead time: 6 weeks to provision reserved burst GPUs and run the canary. We recommend confirming by 01 Oct to hit a Nov window.

Pricing snapshot (high level):
- Year 1: Base commit = 60% of forecast (monthly true-up threshold at 85% of base).
- Year 2: Base commit = 100% of forecast (quarterly step-ups applied automatically per MAP schedule).
- Safety valve true-up cap = up to 20% of annual committed increase; additional overages billed at standard overage rate.

If helpful, Marissa and I can produce two short PO language snippets (standard amendment and alternative amortized true-up). Grace — do you want me to drop those into the MAP?

Thanks — happy to review with procurement on a short call.

— Karthik
VP, Enterprise Sales Operations
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
